source: the camera of the skim over the ring plane and how the light changes with the camera's height. Lengths in planet radii, angles in degrees. Read by plan.ts and set.ts.

pose.note: the middle of the skim: where the camera stands (azimuth from the Sun's side, radius of its foot on the plane, height), and how it looks (the globe this far right of the view axis, tilt down, roll) and the height of its lens (vfov, degrees). Fitted by assets-src/saturn/code/pose_fit2.py so that the true world lies on the approved close image: the lit limb of the globe (within 15 pixels of 1920 on the rays from 80 to 165 degrees round its middle, 6.6 as the root of the mean square) and the left horizon of the rings (within 5 pixels from x 4 to 836, 6.0 over all of it), with the edge of night and the two edges of the dark gap as lighter terms. The foot of the lit globe of the approved image lies 55 to 65 pixels above the line where this globe meets the plane (x 1040 to 1140): no flat plane round a globe gives that, so no pose fits limb, horizon and foot together; the foot is closed by ring matter instead (inner, below).

path.note: travel over the whole skim: forward is the length of the way along the view axis on the plane that the straight skim has over its whole time; descent is the height at the start over the height at the end. The height falls by the same share in every frame and the speed over the plane goes with the height, so the sheet passes under the lens at the same number of pixels a frame, all the way to the bend (bend, below), where the direction of the way turns and the rule of the speed stays; side is the travel sideways, yawDeg and pitchDeg the turn of the camera over the skim. The straight skim heads 28 degrees to the left of its view axis (forward 1.36 cos 28, side minus 1.36 sin 28: eight tenths of the length of way of the pose before, since the lens of this pose stands lower and looks through a longer lens, so the sheet passes at about the same number of pixels a frame): at the judged frame the lens then runs more along the ringlets than across them (5.889e-3 radii a frame across in place of 8.521e-3), and the smear of the film's shutter lies along the lines (ruling 2 of mail 577). The pose at the middle of the judged frame's shutter is the pose it was.

bend.note: the end of the skim (ruling d196): the way of the lens bends from the push at the globe into a track across the plane and on into the pull back, so the rise takes its motion and the lens never stops and turns back. from and to: the shares of the skim, from its middle, between which the direction turns (the judged frame is the middle, its take ends at 0.0014; 0.0111 is two frames past it, 0.489 two frames before the end of the skim). turnDeg: the turn of the heading over the plane toward the right of the lens, where the globe is (190 and the 28 degrees the skim heads left of its view axis, so the way ends on the heading it ended on). liftDeg: the angle of the way to the plane at the end (it starts at the descent of the skim, 10.7 degrees down). turn and lift: the pace of each (plan.ts Pace: the shares of the bend between which its rate is level, and the shares over which its turns are rounded). steps: the steps the way is summed in. All the way the speed of the lens is the same share of its height over the plane as in the straight skim.

light.note: exposure of the globe and of the rings and how much of its colour the ice keeps, first in the hold and then in the skim, blended by the logarithm of the camera's height between the two heights (the lower height is the skim); the strengths of the ladder of ringlets are blended the same way (ringfine.json near). tint: the factor on the colour of the dense and of the thin rings, far in the hold and near in the skim: both approved images have the thin rings brighter and less red than the model's ink, and the close has its dense rings a little darker. halo: the factor on the scale height and on the brightness of the glow outside the globe's limb. halo.day: the two cosines of the Sun's angle between which the day light of that glow comes in with the lens near the plane (with the lens high the haze keeps its own, look.ts shell dayFrom and dayTo; the share between them is the one share of the globe's light, by the height of the lens, grade.ts bodyShare and hazeDayAt, in the kept set and in the model alike): near the sheet the glow draws back toward the Sun and dies away along the limb well before the terminator, as in the approved close, where the limb far from the Sun is a clean edge. dusk: on the globe the light between these two cosines of the Sun's angle (from, to) is cut down by a smooth step by amount, one number at every height of the lens, and that number is 0: the boundary of day and night is the body's own, the same in the hold and in the skim, and does not move over the clouds as the lens comes down or goes up; dusk.lean: see its own note. dusk.night is the factor on the floor of light the night side keeps, and it alone follows heights of its own (dusk.nightHeights, planet radii, the lower the skim; grade.ts nightShare): the night side keeps the light of the hold while the dust inside the inner rim comes in over it and sinks only low in the skim, where the lens goes slowly. dusk.grey: how far the night side is grey rather than the colour of the clouds in the last red light; the share follows the cut of the light to the power greyPower, so with a power above one the colour goes later than the light and the last light keeps its brown. The pairs of the dusk (night, grey) are the value with the lens high and the value with the lens near the plane, and the share between the two of grey is the share of the grade of the rings (grade.ts: by the height of the lens over the ring plane between the two heights of sky.heights), in the kept set and in the model alike; it does not follow globeNear. flatten: the brightness of the dense rings averaged over width radii, over pivot (no further from 1 than reach times or one over reach), is raised to power: near the sheet the broad zones are evener, as in the approved close. flatten.bands: the power on the brightness of a band of the dense rings (the model averaged over band radii) over that of its zone (averaged over width), far and near, counted no further from 1 than bandReach times: near the sheet the bands stand out less from their zone, as in the approved close; ringlets narrower than a band keep their contrast. dusk.tint: the factor on the colour of the clouds in the low light toward the terminator (colour), in full where the cosine of the Sun's angle is at from or under it and none from to on, by the share of the grade of the rings (none with the lens high): the approved close has that light less red and less blue than the clouds' own colour. tone: see its own note.
light.globeNearNote: the share of the near settings of the globe (its exposure, the halo and the blur of its night side) that shows near the sheet: 0 keeps these of the hold from far to near; the shadow of the rings on the globe stays the kept one with it. The dusk of the globe does not follow this number: it follows the height of the lens (see dusk)

grade.note: the grade of the rings by the height of the lens over the ring plane: none of it at the upper height of the air of the stop (sky.heights) and above, where every height of the hold lies, all of it at the lower and under, where the whole skim lies, between them by the logarithm of the height, eased at both ends; in the kept set and in the model alike, and nothing of it follows the clock or the distance from the lens. The far look of the rings is the tone of the picture of the hold and the near light of the model is fitted to the approved close image; the grade takes the far look to the tone of the near light: outward of the dense ring (between the two radii of zone, planet radii, the ramp lies in the division) the ice darker than pivot sinks by the power toe of its light over pivot, and the ice loses a share of its colour, grey[0] in the dense ring and grey[1] in the thin zones. In the far look and in the near light alike the brightest ice is held under ceiling (the light over the root of one plus the square of the light over the ceiling) with its colour kept. dense: the factor on the far look of the dense ring before the ceiling, which takes it to the tone of the dense ring in the approved close (the near light of the dense ring has its own factor, tint.near.dense). view: outward of the dense ring the far look and the near light alike are raised by the cosine of the view to the normal of the plane over cosine, to the power power, where the view is steeper than cosine, and at most most times: seen from near the plane the thin rings keep their brightness toward the lens as a plane of ice does, as in the approved close

radial.note: the tone of the rings by radius with the lens in the skim: the factors on red, green and blue at the radii first, first plus step and so on (planet radii; straight lines between; inward of the first radius the first factors hold and outward of the last the last, 1), by the same share of the height as the rest of the grade. Measured by assets-src/saturn/code/ring_radial.py: the middle value of the scene light of the approved close image over that of the model at frame 3720, per ring of radii of the fitted pose, on the lit sheet where no globe lies in front and where the law of the low view (low, below) leaves the light alone; held between 0.4 and 4.5 (between 0.55 and 1.8 outward of radius 1.56, where the ice is dense, and on a straight line across the dark gap from 1.92 to 2.10, whose edges lie at other radii in the approved image than in the model: the table carries the broad tone, never the place of an edge) and evened over three knots; then fitted once more by assets-src/saturn/code/ring_tone.py on the frame at the final tier, where the grains of the near rings stand as the film shows them: a broad factor on that table, one free value every 0.06 radii from 1.27 outward with straight lines between in the logarithm, none inside the dark gap, within the same bounds, the one which brings the frame nearest to the approved close image in the mean absolute level of the frame. Inward of the inner rim (the knots from 1.03 to 1.25) the table holds one factor: the sheet there is the dust (inner), which the approved close image has in slate grey, and the factors measured there followed the glow of the globe and the edge of its shadow, not the dust; the one factor is set against the approved close image at frame 3720.

fine.note: the ringlets' amplitude by radius (d323): its own term of the one law by radius, apart from the level. The tone above moves the level of a zone; this moves the contrast of the ringlets inside it: the light of a pixel over the light of its zone (a zone: wide footprints of the pixel along the radius), held inside ratio, is raised to the power gain holds at that radius (grade.ts iceFine and iceRinglets; the far look of sheet.ts and kept/rings.ts on their profile, the near look of sheet.ts and grains.ts on the model's profile and its ladder). It has the share of the tone by height (grade.by), so the hold has nothing of it. gain is fit by assets-src/saturn/code/ring_fine.py against the approved close image at frame 3720, final tier: the fine contrast as tools/measure/g17.py counts it, where the ring plane is first on the view; one free value every 0.06 radii from the inner rim out, straight lines between, none inside the gap 1.92 to 2.10, never under 1 (where the film has as much fine contrast as the approved image or more it is left: crisp ringlets are not taken back), never over 1.6. Three steps from a trial of 1.3 at every radius; the last step would move no value by more than 0.018. What stands over 1: 1.6 at 1.27, 1.22 at 1.33, 1.26 at 1.87, 1.24 at 2.17, 1.6 at 2.23 and 2.29; at 1.27, 2.23 and 2.29 the film still has 0.62, 0.77 and 0.84 of the approved image's fine contrast. Measured on the final frame 3720 with and without the term: the reader's median over all 62 tiles 1.0022 against 0.8427 (main 0.9739), apart from the nine tiles of the foot 1.1537 against 1.0205 (main 1.0329); the frame's number outside the two parts read apart 21.8276 against 21.3247 (main 22.0921): contrast that does not lie where the approved image has it costs level, 0.50 here.

low.note: the thin inner ring by the angle of the view, with the lens in the skim: in the approved close image the inner ring and the dust inside it are as bright as the dense ring where the view meets the plane steeply, near the lens, and fall to near black where it runs low over the plane, on the far side by the globe. So inward of zone[0] (planet radii; none of it outward of zone[1]) the light of the sheet is multiplied by the cosine of the view to the normal of the plane over cosine, to the power power, never under least and never over 1; by the same share of the height as the rest of the grade, so none of it in the hold, and by the angle alone, never by the clock.

by.note: the share of the tone by radius (radial) and of the thin inner ring by the view (low) at the heights of the lens over the ring plane (planet radii), straight lines in the logarithm of the height between the knots: none at the upper height of the air of the stop (sky.heights) and above, where every height of the hold lies, all at the height of the approved close image and under. The tone is applied as the factor to the power of the share. It is the largest change of the grade (the thin inner ring gains several times its light), so it does not come in over the heights of the grade alone but over the whole way down, and the shares are set so that the lens passes equal shares in equal times on the fastest way through these heights, the rise: the pattern of the rings then changes slowly on every frame of the dive and of the rise. It follows the height alone, the same way down and up.

body.note: the one share of the light of the globe by the height of the lens over the ring plane (planet radii): none at the upper height and above, where every height of the hold lies (the hold stands at 2.038 to 2.204 in the solved view of the hold, fit.json), all at the lower and under, where frame 3720 lies (0.3622); between them a step in the logarithm of the height, flat at both ends, the same on the way down and on the way up (grade.ts bodyShare): straight lines in the logarithm of the height between the knots heights, with the share at each. The two approved pictures show two terminators (level of the clouds at the cosine -0.14 of the Sun's angle: 85 in the hero, 15 in the close image), and both are kept: everything of the globe that differs between them (dusk amount, lean, night floor, grey, tint, the tone by latitude, the calm of the small features and the day edge of the haze) follows this share and no other, so no number of the globe has a window of heights of its own. The knots are made by assets-src/saturn/code/body_pace.py from the measured answer of the globe (body_response.json). The level on the screen does not follow the share in a straight line: a place in the twilight at 8 to 16 N makes 41 percent of its 81 levels in the first 16 percent of the share, one at 26 to 40 N nearly none of it early. With the share an eased straight line in the logarithm of the height (ease 0.1) the same places of the body changed by up to 2.82 levels from one film frame to the next on the rise (8 to 16 N at the cosine -0.14, frame 3819 to 3820), with a cubic step by more, and before the one share, when the dusk, the lean, the grey, the tint and the tone followed the grade of the rings (heights 0.6 to 2.2) and the night floor heights of its own (0.36 to 0.6), by as much as 38 levels between the frames 3830 and 3838. The knots lay the share along the rise, the fastest passage of the lens through these heights, so that the place of the body that changes fastest changes evenly from frame to frame, with eased ends; the dive passes the same heights in more frames and changes less. By the measured answer the knots read 1.69 levels a frame at the most on the rise, 1.68 in the skim and 1.21 on the dive; what the film itself reads with them stands in assets-src/saturn/NOTES-CODE.md.

lean.note: near the sheet the boundary of day and night on the globe stands more upright, as in the approved close image, where it lies later by the equator and earlier toward the pole than the Sun of the film draws it: the cosine of the Sun's angle on the clouds gets low more by the equator and falls by fall toward the pole, between the two sines of the latitude lat; times the one share of the globe's light by the height of the lens (grade.ts bodyShare, leanAt), so none of it in the hold. Measured on rows of frame 3720 against the approved close image: the place where the light has fallen to the floor lay 30 to 40 px too far toward the Sun at the rows 540 and under and 30 to 45 px too far from it at the rows 140 to 300 (one radian of the globe is about 566 px there).

tone.note: the factor on the colour of the clouds by latitude near the sheet: gain, one knot of three numbers (red, green, blue, scene linear) per step degrees of latitude from first, either side of the equator, straight lines between the knots and flat outside them (the knots stand in a row of texels, grade.ts latToneRow), raised to the one share of the globe's light by the height of the lens (grade.ts bodyShare, the knots of light.body: a step in the logarithm of the height from the hold to the skim), so it is 1 with the lens high and the hold keeps its picture. Measured by assets-src/saturn/code/lat_tone.py: the lit globe of the approved close image over the lit globe of frame 3720 by whole degrees, in two passes (assets-src/saturn/code/lat_tone_raw.json), then smoothed along the latitude with a bell of 10 degrees, the knots under 12 degrees taken as the one at 12 (lat_tone.py --smooth); then one pass more on the final frame drawn with that table (lat_tone.py --again: the table times the plain measure of that frame, assets-src/saturn/code/lat_tone_again.json, smoothed in the same way, so the table stays as smooth as it was), and once more in the same way on the final frame drawn after the globe's light was laid again in the solved view of the hold (globe-light.bin; the measure is assets-src/saturn/code/lat_tone_solved.json): the tone comes with the height of the lens, so it changes the broad palette of the globe by latitude and no band of it. The approved close is pale cream with a grey blue band near the top limb and calm bands; the map of the hold is more orange and busier. calm: near the sheet the small features of the map stand out less: the map is mixed by amount with itself averaged over texels of its texels, and the boost of its small features (look.ts globe fine) is taken back by fine; both times the same one share.

outer.note: near the sheet its outer rim is no edge: past the rim (ringfield.json outer) the ice goes on and thins out by two laws that add, each a depth at the rim (the normal optical depth) that falls by e over its length; all of it ends softly between the two radii of end. inset: the colour of that ice is read this far inside the rim. inkBy: how fast that colour takes over as the lens comes near. All of it shows by how near the lens is, none in the hold. rimReach: the brightness of that ice is the middle value of the model's knots from so many insets inside the rim to one inset inside it. grow: how that ice comes with the nearness of the lens in the dive: its depth is times the nearness to the power depth and its two lengths are times the nearness to the power length (no shorter than the share least), so it grows outward from the rim and no band of it shows away from the rim first; in the skim the nearness is 1 and all of it is there.

bands.note: the ice past the rim lies in ringlets of its own: three sets of plateaus of these widths (waves, in radii). At the rim all of them are open; the share that is a gap grows to gap over the distance over past the rim. width: how soft the edge of a gap is, as a share of the range of levels. soft: the least softness of a plateau's edge in cells; filter: that softness in footprints. floor: the share of the depth a gap keeps. lines: the strength of the thin lines at the edges of the plateaus. seed and shift: which plateaus.

inner.note: The thin sheet inside the inner rim (ringfield.json inner) is one body with the ring: the same matter with the same depth and the same ice at every height of the lens, in the hold, the dive, the skim and the rise alike. One law covers it and the ring: the cover of a point of the plane for a ray is 1 - exp(-tau(r) / |sin e|), tau the depth straight through the plane at the radius r and e the angle of the ray to the plane. Nothing of it follows the height of the lens, the distance or the clock. depth: tau at the rim and at the cloud tops (radius 1), a straight line between them. fade: the length inward of the rim over which the sheet ends, so that it lies inside the rim alone. ice: the sheet is dark ice of its own; where it is too deep to see through it returns this share of what the ice of the thin inner ring at the radius like returns there, the same at every radius. So against the black of the hold its own light is small, and in front of the lit globe of the skim, where the flat view runs a long way through it, it is a veil that takes light away. The same depth shades the globe behind it on the Sun's ray (grade.ts dustShadeAt) and is shaded by the globe (sheet.ts globeShadow); neither has a share of its own. The sheet takes no part in the grade of the rings by the height of the lens (light.grade). inset: the colour of the sheet's ice is read this far outside the rim. bands: the plateaus of its depth, as past the outer rim (over: the length inward of the rim over which they come in, gap: the share of them that is thinner, floor: the share of its depth a thinner one keeps). rings: the finer ringlets of its light, about the same mean (waves: their three widths, seed, gap: the share that is dark, floor: the share of its light a dark one keeps, amount: how far they show, soft, filter, lines, width: their edges as sheet.ts sheetBandsOf takes them). air: the sheet by the globe lies in the globe's twilight, where the Sun's light comes to it through the globe's air (depth straight up from the ground, and the height over which the air thins by e; grade.ts dustAir). end: the radius the plane is drawn from. foot: a layer of dust on the globe itself by the plane (depth on the view at the plane, the two heights over the plane between which it ends, its colour); its depth is 0, the film holds no such layer. The measurements stand in assets-src/saturn/NOTES-CODE.md.
inner.iceNote: the thin sheet inside the inner rim is not drawn: depth 0 (ruled, d323). The numbers below it stay for the record of what was tried: depth is the depth at the rim and at the cloud tops, a straight line between, the same at every height of the lens; cover of a point for a ray = 1 - exp(-depth / sine of the ray to the plane), the law of the whole ring; ice is what its ice returns of the light the bright rings return at the same depth; join the two widths over which the sheet ends at the rim. Measured at the final tier, mean absolute level against the approved pictures at the frames 3465 and 3720 (main 4.7807 and 27.7989): no sheet 4.7768 and 28.0406; depth 0.05 with ice 0.05 (dark ice) 4.7784 and 28.0507; depth 0.05 with ice 1 (bright ice) 4.9556 and 27.7928. No sheet is the best of the three at the hold and better than the dark sheet at both frames; the bright sheet gains 0.25 at 3720 and loses 0.18 at the hold, where it puts bright ringlets on the black that the approved hero has between the globe and the rings. The approved close image has lit ring matter where the plane inward of the rim lies at this pose (its rings cross the globe about 6 degrees higher than a true plane does): one matter in one light cannot give that without filling the gap of the hold, so that part of frame 3720 is read apart

lens.note: the field of view in the dive and in the rise. moves: for each of the two moves, 'distance' or 'pace'. distance: the field of view is a function of the eye's distance from the planet's centre and of nothing else. It is the hold's lens at the distance of the last frame of the hold and beyond, the skim's lens (pose.vfov) at the distance of the first frame of the skim and nearer (the skim itself goes on inward with that lens, so its frames keep their picture), and between the two the tangent of half the field is a power of the distance. ease: the lengths, in the natural logarithm of the distance, over which the exponent of that power rises from nothing at the skim's end of the span and falls to nothing at the hold's end, so the growth of the globe's disc has no step where the law begins and where it ends (without the first the rate of the disc would jump at the first frame of the skim, where the eye is still coming in). The second is short (0.001 is the way of the first two and a half frames of the dive): the eye itself starts slowly out of the hold's drift, so an exponent that stands at its level from the start opens the lens in step with the eye, and the disc's rate rises at every frame up to 3569. A longer one costs the path: while the exponent still rises the lens gains on the eye's own way, which moves the picture at the place the path reader reads downward while the lens draws it to the middle of the screen, and the picture's speed there rises and falls back. Measured: on the level alone 0.004 let it fall by 0.047 of its mean from 3544 to 3551 (limit 0.03; the reader names only the largest fall, so the fall in the middle hid this one); with the swell 0.003 gives about 0.015, 0.008 about 0.06, 0.015 to 0.04 between 0.05 and 0.12. From 0.055 on the fall is gone again because the lens then waits for the eye, but the disc's rate overshoots (0.283 percent a frame at 3555, 0.212 at 3562) and changes by 0.032 a frame at 3544. swell: about the distance at (planet radii) the exponent stands higher by gain of its level, and the swell falls off to nothing over reach of the natural logarithm of the distance on either side as half a cosine (it must lie inside the span, the plan throws if not). Why (MAIL 1508): between 4.58 and 3.75 radii (frames 3568 to 3603) the eye's own way moves the picture on the screen least, because the turn of the dive passes its still point there (at the reader's place with the lens held: 2.9 px a frame at 3573, 0.7 at 3591, 3.9 at 3612). An exponent of one level opened the lens an even 0.13 degrees a frame through it, so the picture's speed at the place fell from 0.949 of its mean at 3575 to 0.726 at 3588 and surged to 1.915 at 3610, in steps of up to 0.085 a frame: four red lines of the path part. With the swell the lens opens up to 0.174 degrees a frame there (frame 3586) and covers what the eye's way leaves out: the speed falls by 0.014 of its mean at most (frame 3580; 0.015 at rate 2), and its largest step is 0.068 (frame 3623, the slowing into the skim, 0.073 before; 0.069 at rate 2; limits 0.03 and 0.08). The price, measured on the path: the disc's growth dips from 0.273 percent a frame at 3569 to 0.104 at 3586 and comes back to 0.281 at 3604, where the level alone gave an even 0.236. It grows at every frame of the dive, and its rate changes by 0.016 a frame at most (frame 3577; the level alone 0.022 at 3543). A smaller dip is not to be had while the eye and the turn stay: for each 0.01 degrees a frame the lens opens faster at 3588 the speed there gains about 0.12 px a frame and the disc's growth loses about 0.03 percent a frame. The eye, the turn and the way of the dive are untouched; the lens differs from the level's by 0.35 degrees at most (frame 3597, the disc 1.0 percent smaller) and by 0.21 at the judged 3567 (the disc 0.65 percent larger). So the disc grows at every frame the eye comes nearer. pace: the field of view goes from the lens of the motion before the move to the lens of the motion after it by the pace of the move's turn (handover view), a function of the time. The rise keeps the pace: its eye crosses the whole span of the law in 34 frames at its largest speed, so there the law would let the disc shrink fast, then slowly, then fast again, where by the pace it shrinks at every frame at a rate that changes evenly.
lens.outNote: the lens at the end of the rise, which the flight out takes over and keeps: the lens of the flights between the stops and of the next hold. The hold of this stop stands on the lens of the fit (fit.json, vfovDeg), wider than this; the rise goes from the skim's lens to this one by its pace, so the flight out begins on the lens it ends on and a Sun that passes its frame is met by the same half frame as in every other flight

handover.note: the dive and the rise: one flight through one world, no picture is swapped and no cover is drawn. at: the share of the dive or the rise at which the engine changes from the view in the frame of the globe to the view in the frame of the skim (both show the same world from the same lens); The sky does not follow that change nor any clock (sky below). Each move (the dive, the rise) is one move in four measures, each with one pace (plan.ts Pace): the rate of the measure goes from its rate in the motion before the move up to one largest value and down to its rate in the motion after it, by a steady change a frame on both sides; peak is the share of the move at which the rate turns at the top, or two shares between which the rate stays level at its largest value (a level top), and round the share of the move over which each of its turns is rounded: one share for all turns, or one for each turn in order (three with one peak: the start, the top, the end; four with a level top: the start, the two ends of the level, the end). reach: the distance of the lens to the globe's surface (its logarithm). climb: the height over the ring plane (its logarithm); in the rise it turns before the reach: the lens, which draws back from the end of the skim on (path.bend), lifts off the plane first and then draws back faster. round: the angle of the foot of the lens round the globe. view: the turn of the camera from the one motion's to the other's, and the field of view with it. rise.carry: the speed over the drift of the way out (planet radii a second, on that drift's own line) with which the rise ends: the rise ends in the middle of its brake, it does not speed up at its end, and the travel of the engine takes that speed and that brake over (src/director/film.ts carryOf), so the picture does not come to rest between the rise and the travel; the place at the end of the rise is the same with or without it. place.ahead: the place the tool watches is the point of the ring plane this far ahead of the foot of the lens at the middle of the skim.

kept.note: the approach and the hold are drawn by the set of the kept build (kept/), the skim, the rise and the way out by the ring model. In the dive the kept set first lets its picture of the hold go over to its plain radial profile (its own weights, by the lens's distance from the hero pose). Then the picture goes from the kept set to the model by the height of the lens over the ring plane and by nothing else: between the two heights of heights (planet radii, by the logarithm) every take of a frame draws one of the two whole scenes from the same lens, the share of takes of the model rises by a smooth step from 0 at the upper height to 1 at the lower, and the takes of each scene are spread over the open shutter by stride (a take is the model's when its number times stride, modulo the count, plus one half, over the count, is under the share; strides lists the candidates, the first without a common factor with the count is used). Above the upper height every take is the kept set, under the lower every take is the model, at any rate of capture. The upper height lies under the height at which the kept set's layout has become the plain profile (hero distance 1.6, height about 1.05). Through those heights the model draws the sheet with the far look: the kept set's own formula on the kept profile (sheet.ts), so the two scenes are one picture there. far: between these two heights of the lens over the ring plane (by the logarithm) the far look gives way to the model's own light and the lens's closeness begins to count (the far look alone above the upper, the model's light in full under the lower), the same way down and up. close: how much of its own closeness the kept set keeps (0: it stays the far picture). view: the cosine of the view to the normal at which the kept profile's opacity is the sheet's own (as in kept/rings.ts).
kept.reachNote: one look from far to near: under the far heights the sheet keeps the far look wherever it lies farther from the lens than the second distance (planet radii) and has the light of the model, with the ringlets, the sand and the grains it adds, nearer than the first, by the logarithm of the distance between
kept.lawNote: the one law of cover (ruled 12:23 UTC): the ring is one body at every height of the lens, so every view ray that crosses its plane is covered by 1 - exp(-depth / sine), sine that of the angle between the ray and the plane, floored only against the division (floor). The depth at a radius is the kept ring's own: what gives the kept opacity at the sine of the hold's eye (view: the sine from the lens of the judged hold frame 3465 to the ring where it passes in front of the globe, 0.52 at the inner rim, 0.55 at radius 1.5, 0.59 at radius 1.9). model: the sine at which assets-src/saturn/code/ring_model.py turned the kept opacity into the model's depth, so the model near the sheet counts its depth view / model times and reads the same law. The kept set (kept/rings.ts), the far look and the model near the sheet (sheet.ts) all read it: no share, no window, no height of the lens and no clock is in the cover. In front of the lit globe the kept ring lets 0.015 of the globe through at the sine of the hold's eye (kept/look.ts sheetThrough): that is the ring's own opacity there, and the same law carries it to every sine, in all three
kept.seamNote: the thin line outside the outer edge (the look's arc) is drawn at a footprint of at most this many times the footprint of the true radius of the plane, and only inside the span of the profile. At the reach of the profile the hero's shape ends, so the bent radius jumps there and the frame to frame measure of the footprint was huge on the pixel pairs that lie across that jump: the arc then read the coarsest level of the profile and drew a line of dashes there that moved with the pixel grid from frame to frame. Elsewhere the footprint is as before
kept.aloneNote: for the proof of the handing over only: kept or model draws that scene alone in every take from the hold's end on; empty in the film

globeFine.note: the fine structure of the globe's bands near the lens, from functions under the texels of the 8192 map (globe.ts bandFine): streaks along the bands, value noise over cells of latitude and longitude in octaves that halve. reach: the structure is whole where the surface is nearer to the lens than the first distance and absent beyond the second (planet radii, by the logarithm), so the hold and the dive do not have it. cell: the cell of latitude of the first octave in radians; stretch: how many times longer a cell is along the band than across; octaves: how many; amount: the strength of the first octave on the logarithm of the cloud colour, fall: the factor on it per octave; bend: by how many cells an octave is shifted across the band by the octave before it; pixels: the width of a cell in pixels (one over the cells that a pixel step crosses) up to which an octave is absent and from which it is whole, so the finest octave at half strength or more has between one and two cells a pixel; tint: the strength per colour, the blue more so that a dark streak is warmer; zone: some belts are more streaked than others, the strength runs between the first and the second value with a value of its own per cell of latitude of the third value (radians); relief: toward the terminator the low sun sets the relief of the cloud tops off more strongly, the strength grows by the first value where the cosine of the Sun's angle is at or under the second and not at all from the third on; wide: the sharpening of the map's small features (showcase look.fine) sets them off against a neighbourhood of so many pixels in the far view; near the lens that neighbourhood is never fewer than this many texels of the map, so the features of the map keep their contrast when a texel grows to a pixel and the globe has no brighter tone where it is nearest; seed. The texels view counts, only where the structure is whole, the cells a pixel of the finest octave that is drawn at half strength or more, from the same coordinates and weights as the picture.

sky.note: one sky for the stop: the film's own star field, in the far view and in the skim alike, and nothing of it follows the clock. hero: the picture of the sky of the hold belongs to the path the lens flies in the hold; it shows in full on that path and leaves with the distance of the lens from it (planet radii, to the nearest point of the path): none of it is left from the distance reach on, and between it falls by a smooth step of the distance over reach to the power power, which spreads the fall evenly over the first part of the dive; slack is the distance under which the lens counts as on the path and chords the number of chords the path is measured with. So it is gone before the engine changes the view and never comes back in the rise (plan.ts skyProof stops the build if a path breaks that). heights: the two heights of the lens over the ring plane (planet radii, by the logarithm, the lower is the skim) between which the air of the stop comes in, the same way down and up, and power the power on its course between them (under 1: it comes in early below the upper height, so the stars the picture of the hold uncovers are dimmed as they show, and settles at the lower; the upper height lies under every height of the hold, plan.ts skyProof stops the build if it does not): near is the share of the exposure of the stars that is left at the lower height (extinction), lift: the stars of the flight (the many faint stars of the film's open sky, which the engine brings in through the rise after its change of view) come in by the height of the lens over the ring plane and not by the clock: their level is a smooth step of 1 - (1 - share)^lift.power, share the way between the two heights of lift.heights (planet radii); the lens leaves the rise with speed (handover rise.carry) and climbs on through its end, so with the power 1 the level is a smooth step of the height itself and is whole with no slope left at the upper height, no kink of the level of the sky where the travel takes the flight over (plan.ts skyLiftAt undoes the engine's own course so that this is the level shown); the lower height lies over every height at which the hold and the dive are flown, so it is one function of the height going down and coming up (none of them at any height of the hold or of the dive, none at the same heights in the rise), and over the height of the lens at the engine's change of view in the rise; the upper lies under its height at the end of the rise (plan.ts skyProof stops the build if not). glow the faint light of the fine dust over the plane that lies under the stars there (veil.ts): color in linear light at the exposure of the stop, plane how much brighter it is along the ring plane than high over it, fall the sine of the angle over the plane at which that gain has fallen to 1 over e. halo: the light of the lit globe thrown forward by that dust, a wide soft glow round the lit limb: color at the limb, fallDeg the angle from the limb at which it has fallen to 1 over e, lit the two cosines of the angle between the nearest limb and the Sun between which it comes in (none at the dark limb). look: the look of the sky of the skim, named to the engine's sky (src/space/sky.ts nameSkyLook) every time the set is drawn, with the weight of the air of the stop (all of it at the lower of heights, none at the upper, so it is one function of the height going down and coming up and nothing of it follows the clock): look the look of the band of the sky (0 the plain one), even how far the crowding of the stars gives way to one even field (1 all the way: the field of the approved close image), stars the gain on the stars at the skim against the open sky (the air leaves near of their exposure, so their level at the skim is stars times near; plan.ts starsAt names the gain on the way so that the level of a faint star runs straight between the two heights and does not swell), cap the brightness no star goes over at the skim.
